- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment shifts from neutral to positive, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.53, 0.00, 0.53), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
